answer: One concrete mechanism: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because ferrous only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, reef is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any lotus approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
